A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Code-as-Monitor and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplements. Renumbered sections and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original robotic experiments across three simulators and a real-world setting, segmentation evaluations, and ablations in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds segmentation-module and failure-detection-mode ablations in Appendix E, Table 11.

M1.justification: The Generator/Painter/Monitor architecture, ConSeg training objectives, geometric elements, and tracking-based monitoring remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 newly documents code validation and threshold selection as implementation clarifications; it does not establish a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training data, simulator and real-world tasks, segmentation benchmarks, and supplementary out-of-distribution examples are retained. The new ablations reuse the existing OmniGibson tasks Slot Pen, Stow Book, and Pour Tea.

E2.justification: LISA and PixelLM, already compared on segmentation in Table 5, are newly evaluated as replacement segmentation modules in the end-to-end OmniGibson comparison in Table 11. Existing baseline membership in Tables 1–10 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 11 adds controlled evaluation configurations that substitute segmentation models or enable only proactive or reactive detection. These configurations reuse the stated OmniGibson protocol and success-rate/execution-time metrics; the original benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds two focused ablation sets: ConSeg versus LISA/PixelLM within the complete system, and separate versus combined failure-detection modes. The earlier multiview, element-construction, geometric-abstraction, and training-data ablations remain.

E5.justification: Existing seed/trial information and confidence-interval reporting are retained, including five CLIPort seeds and 95% confidence intervals in the detailed CLIPort and real-world results. Table 11 reports point estimates, consistent with earlier ablation tables, without introducing a new statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–10 retain their numerical results. Table 11 adds ablation results: for Stow Book, the full system reports 65.00% success and 93.08 seconds, versus 50.00% and 109.47 seconds for proactive-only detection and 57.50% and 147.95 seconds for reactive-only detection.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 and the constraint/segmentation formulation are unchanged. The added discussions introduce no mathematical definitions, formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: unified reactive/proactive detection, constraint elements, and code-based monitoring for closed-loop robotics. The headline claims of 28.7% higher success and 31.8% lower execution time are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A explains proactive monitoring through constraints on future states, qualifies unseen-object segmentation as weaker than in-distribution performance, and identifies threshold sensitivity across diverse conditions as unexplored. Appendix E interprets the new ablations as evidence of complementary detection modes. The original limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly describes branch/path checks and regeneration of erroneous monitor code, plus thresholds obtained from a manually initialized knowledge base or VLM knowledge. It also clarifies when segmentation runs. Existing training details, hardware information, and the monitor-generation prompt remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The references add RoboBrain, SoFar, RoboFactory, and NavigateDiff while removing four works, including Scaling Up and VLSBench. Appendix A.1 expands the comparison with ReKep's keypoint extraction and code generation. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. v3 adds supplementary discussion and ablation sections, moves the former Appendix D limitations to Appendix A.3, renumbers subsequent sections, corrects the placement of the Section 4.4 heading, and adds acknowledgments and limited wording/affiliation edits.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 11 and repositions existing displays, including Table 8 and Figure 11, as text reflows. Figures 1–24 retain their substantive content. Table 2 also corrects the label 'Solt Pen' to 'Slot Pen'.

improvement.justification: Table 11 supplies direct evidence for the segmentation choice and the benefit of combining detection modes, while Appendix A improves implementation transparency and applicability qualifications. These are useful, targeted gains. Their scope remains limited: the new ablations provide no uncertainty estimates, and threshold sensitivity is explicitly left unexplored.
